<h2>SherlockEQ 0.1.4</h2>

<p>
  A look-and-feel release. A new app icon, a Liquid Glass pass over the
  whole window on macOS&nbsp;Tahoe, and Reference Mode promoted to the
  title bar so you can A/B against the source from anywhere — not just
  the Equalizer. Under the hood, the audio engine now shrugs off the
  transient device hiccups that could leave it silent after a wake or a
  route change.
</p>

<h3>Added</h3>

<ul>
  <li>
    <strong>New app icon.</strong>
    A dimensional gold magnifying glass over a frequency spectrum —
    sharper at every size from the Dock down to the menu bar.
  </li>
  <li>
    <strong>Reference Mode in the title bar.</strong>
    The Bypass toggle moved out of the Equalizer and into the window
    toolbar, so you can drop to the unprocessed source from any
    screen. It's renamed <em>Reference Mode</em> to match the popover
    and ⌘B — one control, three places, same wording. Goes red when
    active so you always know you're hearing raw audio.
  </li>
</ul>

<h3>Changed</h3>

<ul>
  <li>
    <strong>Liquid Glass chrome (macOS&nbsp;Tahoe).</strong>
    On macOS&nbsp;26 the toolbar controls now render as separate Liquid
    Glass clusters, the notice banner and layer chips pick up the glass
    material, and detail content softly fades as it scrolls under the
    toolbar. Sonoma and Sequoia keep their existing look.
  </li>
  <li>
    <strong>Steadier sidebars.</strong>
    Both the navigation sidebar and the monitor gutter are now pinned to
    a fixed 240&nbsp;pt and stay put — no width drift between launches,
    and the primary navigation no longer collapses out from under you.
  </li>
</ul>

<h3>Fixed</h3>

<ul>
  <li>
    <strong>Silent engine after sleep or a route change.</strong>
    When the audio device reports a transient "try again" error — common
    while a sample-rate or output-route change is still settling, or
    right after waking from sleep — SherlockEQ now retries the engine
    start automatically instead of surfacing an error and going quiet.
  </li>
</ul>

<h3>Not a medical device</h3>

<p>
  SherlockEQ is not a healthcare or medical application. It does not
  diagnose, treat, measure, or monitor any hearing condition, tinnitus,
  or disability. For concerns about your hearing, consult a doctor,
  audiologist, or licensed healthcare professional.
</p>
